issues: Finding 6 overstates what the cited evidence establishes. The analyses support ambiguity in exact discourse-deictic antecedent boundaries and support partial-credit scoring for split/multi-antecedent resolution, but they do not directly validate a general proposition-span evaluation policy in which exact-span scoring should coexist with partial-overlap credit. manual-7743c50805 uses overlap-sensitive measures for annotator agreement, while doi-10-5210-dad-2023-201 concerns partial recovery of split antecedents rather than partial span overlap.

The actionable insight prescribing 'exact-match and partial-overlap measures, explicit zero-link scoring, multi-antecedent partial credit, and separate false-positive and false-negative counts' combines several reasonable engineering choices, but the cited analyses do not jointly establish this exact evaluation package. In particular, separate false-positive/false-negative reporting and general partial-span scoring are not directly supported by the listed findings.

The HIGH-confidence recency finding is somewhat stronger than the corpus warrants. doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778 supports a strong locality prior for discourse deixis, manual-e1981ecd9a supports very local clarification-answer links, and the email/chat studies establish non-local counterexamples. This supports rejecting a universal hard cutoff, but it does not empirically establish a single generally 'strong' recency prior across the heterogeneous target phenomena.

The confidence summary's claim that confidence is HIGH that msgloom specifically 'needs proposition-level, zero-or-many, non-adjacent, ambiguity-preserving response links' mixes directly supported representational phenomena with a product-level architectural conclusion. Zero-link, multi-link, non-adjacency, and ambiguity are individually well supported, but exact proposition-level reply scope in authentic workplace communication remains one of the synthesis's own open gaps. The product requirement is defensible as an engineering inference, but its evidential status should be distinguished from a directly demonstrated workplace result.

The contradiction labeled 'One-to-one alignment assumptions versus observed one-to-many response scope' is useful but should not imply that the residual error in doi-10-1109-icaicta63815-2024-10762999 was caused by its one-to-one constraint. The analysis only establishes that substantial alignment error remained even with gold segmentation; it does not attribute that residual specifically to the matching cardinality assumption.

The synthesis generally handles transfer-domain evidence responsibly, but several actionable recommendations derive jointly from workplace email, customer-service dialogue, multiparty/game dialogue, and abstract-anaphora research. These should remain explicitly labeled as cross-domain design implications rather than direct empirical validation of workplace proposition-level reply scope.
unsupported_claims: Finding 6: 'exact-span evaluation should coexist with partial-overlap credit' is not directly established by the cited analyses as a general response-scope evaluation requirement.

Actionable insight 7: the complete proposed metric package, especially separate false-positive/false-negative counts and generic partial-overlap span scoring, is not directly supported by the cited findings.
Contradiction note on one-to-one alignment: the evidence does not show that the one-to-one assumption caused the residual gold-segmentation alignment error.

Confidence summary: HIGH confidence in a specifically proposition-level msgloom workplace response-link requirement is stronger than the direct workplace evidence; proposition-level workplace approval/rejection/clarification scope is explicitly still open.
notes: All cited paper_ids checked in the synthesis are members of the supplied allow-list. The central empirical synthesis is substantially faithful: partial replies to multi-question turns, unanswered questions, non-adjacent links, zero/one/many alignments, multi-parent discourse structure, composite antecedents, structural ambiguity among multiple interrogatives, and proposition-sensitive acceptance/rejection are all traceable to the supplied analyses. The synthesis also correctly leaves the major direct-workplace proposition-scope questions open and explicitly avoids deriving production thresholds or accuracy guarantees from transfer-domain evidence. The issues are mainly localized overreach in evaluation prescriptions, confidence wording, and one causal implication in the one-to-one-alignment contradiction; they do not invalidate the overall synthesis.
